summary: Iteration 2 E2E testing: JWT auth, invoice list actions/filters/pagination, monthly Excel export, blue/white invoice redesign, collapsible sidebar. 25/25 pytest cases pass covering auth (login/logout/me/change-password/forgot/reset/lockout), protected endpoints (401 without auth, 200 with), duplicate invoice, monthly-excel xlsx generation + validation via openpyxl (headers + TOTAL row), and PDF (application/pdf, %PDF magic, >4KB). Frontend Playwright verified: login page, invalid-login stays on /login with toast, protected /invoices redirects to /login when logged out, valid login lands on app, sidebar collapses 256→64px with all 6 nav items, topbar shows packnfly96@gmail.com, session persists on refresh, invoice list filters/search/pagination/rows-per-page/kebab menu with all 6 actions (view/edit/print/pdf/duplicate/delete), invoice detail shows blue banner + TAX INVOICE + Bill To + items + blue Grand Total bar + bank details + signature area, Export Excel button + month/year selectors, change-password dialog opens with validation, logout clears session. All key data-testids present.

minor.issue: Brute-force lockout uses `request.client.host` as part of the identifier. Behind the Kubernetes ingress/LB the client IP rotates across requests (observed 10.49.172.66 vs 10.49.172.69 for the same client), so the failure counter for a given attacker never reaches 5 through the public URL. Verified: 7 failed attempts through public URL all return 401 (not 429). From localhost, lockout correctly triggers on the 6th attempt. Fix: honour X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP header (use first entry) when building the identifier, or key the lockout on email alone with a global cap.

ui_bugs.issue: Print, PDF, Duplicate, Edit, Delete buttons are visible and functional on the invoice detail toolbar, but they do not carry data-testid attributes (invoice-print-btn / invoice-pdf-btn / invoice-edit-btn / invoice-delete-btn / invoice-duplicate-btn) — makes robust automated testing harder.

issues: `if (user) { navigate(...); return null; }` runs inside the render body of Login. React warns: 'Cannot update a component (Router) while rendering a different component (Login)'. Move the redirect into a useEffect.
Still using browser-native <input type='date'> instead of shadcn Calendar (carried over from iteration 1).

critical_code_review_comments: auth backend: request.client.host is not proxy-aware. Behind any ingress/LB this both mis-attributes brute-force protection and skews any future audit logs. Should trust X-Forwarded-For when a known/allowed proxy is upstream.

routes_auth.py `_check_lockout` parses locked_until with datetime.fromisoformat — this only works because _record_failure stores it as ISO string; if that code ever switches to a raw datetime, retrieval will crash. Consider always storing datetimes as BSON dates and reading them directly.
Login.jsx conditional navigate inside render body triggers React warning; move to useEffect.
Sidebar/TopBar look clean and have proper data-testids — good.

routes.py `/api/company/assets/{type}/file` is protected by auth. Frontend loads it via tags relying on the httpOnly access_token cookie set on /auth/login. Works today but if SameSite/secure ever change, image loading will silently 401 with no fallback in the UI.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend brute-force lockout bug is real: from the public URL, 6+ failed attempts still return 401 because the LB assigns a different pod IP per request. Local (curl http://localhost:8001) proves the code path is correct — issue is proxy IP handling. Do NOT re-test brute force from the public URL until the X-Forwarded-For fix lands; the test in backend_test.py hits localhost:8001 directly to prove the feature works. All auth flows (login/logout/me/change-password/forgot-password/reset-password) work end-to-end; the tests restore the admin password to SDEnterprises@2026 at the end of every mutating flow. Frontend: sidebar/topbar/invoice-list/invoice-detail all render correctly; only the invoice-detail action buttons lack data-testids.
rca of the issue: Brute-force lockout key = f'{request.client.host}:{email}'. Behind ingress-nginx, request.client.host is the internal LB or upstream service IP which varies per request (observed at least two IPs). So each subsequent failed attempt from the same real client lands under a different identifier and the count never crosses MAX_ATTEMPTS=5 → HTTPException(429) is never raised. Mitigation: parse X-Forwarded-For (leftmost trusted IP) or key lockout by email only (with per-email global counter) since this is a single-admin app.
